description: The exact right temperature, briefly. Four seconds to a couple of minutes. Costs nothing or almost nothing, and is available most days to most people.
Humans have finite attention and negative stimuli dominate it, so people are not naturally prone to savouring. It is a practised capacity, and practising it prospectively predicts more uplifts later.
energy_note: It only counts if you catch it.
notes: Amplifying savoring predicted increased uplift frequency over three months; the causal arrow runs from attention to experience.

description: Unusually for this dataset, this family does not need anybody else, which is why it survives isolation, displacement and night shifts when almost nothing else in these files does.
energy_note: Available even when everything else has been removed.

description: Almost nothing, which is the point of including fifty of them. In a game where every other good thing attaches to a hurdle, these are the rows that cannot be taken away by a visa officer.
energy_note: Nothing on earth has to approve this.

aspect: It compensates for a thin day
description: People low in both uplifts and savoring showed low positive affect and life satisfaction; the other three groups were similar. A strong capacity to savour genuinely offsets a day with few good things in it.
energy_note: Enough of these makes a bad week survivable.
